描述_EN: the two dishes pictured here are examples of ceramics probably made at linru, in the henan province of china during the jin dynasty (1115-1234). the craftspeople of both yaozhou and linru used moulds to achieve their intricate surface designs some of the time, avoiding the time consumption and labour intensity hand carving. yaozhou wares were popular for their olive green glazes and their detailed surface designs. a convex ‘hump-mould’ was then made from the master, from which multiple dishes could be made, saving time and resources. during this period, the kilns at linru produced wares that imitated those made at the yaozhou kilns in the neighbouring shaanxi provine. this process began with one master dish carved by hand and fired. these wares appear to be very similar to their yaozhou contemporaries, but their glazes have very slight differences in colour and shine that reveal they were probably fired slightly differently.
描述_ZN: 此图中的两个盘子可能是金代（1115-1234）期间在中国河南省临汝制作的陶瓷的例子。 耀州和临汝的工匠们在某些时候使用模具来实现他们复杂的表面设计，避免了手工雕刻的时间消耗和劳动强度。 耀州器物因其橄榄绿的釉面和细致的表面设计而受到欢迎。 一个凸起的 "驼峰模具 "是由母体制成的，可以用它来制作多个盘子，节省时间和资源。 在这一时期，临汝窑生产的器物模仿了邻近的陕西省耀州窑的器物。 这个过程从一个手工雕刻和烧制的主盘开始。 这些器物看起来与同时代的耀州器非常相似，但它们的釉面在颜色和光泽上有非常细微的差别，显示出它们的烧制方式可能略有不同。
